Samir —

Yes, we can do that. High-level plan:  

1) Evidence manifest: we will produce a compact CSV with three columns: question_id (SIG/CAIQ id), evidence_key (canonical filename), evidence_link (S3 HTTPS URL or presigned PUT/GET). We will include a short evidence_type tag (e.g., soc2-report, config-screenshot, policy-doc).

2) Presigned flows: we can generate short-lived presigned PUT URLs for your intake bucket. Redwood will:  
  - generate pre-signed PUTs scoped to a single-purpose prefix (brightleaf/inbound/<vendor-id>/)
  - TTL default 7 days (configurable)
  - require metadata headers x-rlw-evidence-id and x-rlw-source for traceability

3) Retention & access: objects uploaded to your intake bucket can optionally be scanned and moved to your long-term store; Redwood will mark the manifest entries as "uploaded_by_customer" when presigned PUTs are used.

I attached a draft presign policy (PDF) and a tiny example manifest to this thread. Marcus / Priyom — can you review the appended policy for runtime implications (batch presign rate limits, prefix enforcement) and comment by EOD tomorrow?

I can send the first pass CSV tomorrow morning. If BrightLeaf wants automated daily manifests for incremental changes, we can wire that as well (S3 event + lambda to push a manifest).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Compact evidence handback + presign gating

Looping in technical notes — quick summary of constraints we should surface to BrightLeaf before we issue presigns:  

- Rate limits: presign generation is throttled per-tenant. We can pre-generate batches of 100 presigns per minute; if they want a spike we can request a short burst quota.
- Prefix enforcement: presigns will be scoped to brightleaf/inbound/<vendor-id> and validated server-side to prevent cross-tenant writes.
- Metadata enforcement: we will reject uploads missing the required x-rlw-* headers in the upload request. This is enforced in a lightweight lambda authorizer.
- Size limits: single artifact max 250MB over presign. For larger exports we recommend SFTP or signed multipart uploads (we can coordinate).

Action items for Priyom: can you add the presign header validation lambda to the presign-policy-draft and include the minimal IAM policy snippet? Also flag any KMS usage we should call out for encrypted-at-rest requirement.

Marcus
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
